class.name: JarVoxelUniverse
class.brief_description: Engine singleton: the shared clock, the celestial bodies and their gravity.
class.description: Keeps universe time, places every [JarBodyOrbit] and [JarCelestialBody] for it at the end of each physics frame (after all other nodes, so moved colliders are in place for the next frame), and answers gravity queries. Use it as [code]JarVoxelUniverse[/code] from scripts. The scene as placed (orbits at their time 0 position) is the universe at its start: when the first body enters the tree the clock starts at 0, and the first anchor stays exactly where it was placed. Time is an integer count of physics ticks times [code]jar_voxel_terrain/universe/time_scale[/code], plus [code]universe/start_time[/code]: orbits and spin are functions of it, so they never drift and are the same on every machine with the same tick. Physics runs in the frame of the [i]anchor[/i]: the body whose sphere of influence the first [JarVoxelViewer] (else the camera) is in (the smallest one: a moon's inside its planet's, see [method JarCelestialBody.get_sphere_of_influence]), else the strongest pull among the bodies on no orbit, or [method set_anchor_override]. With [code]gravity/drive_space_gravity[/code] on, the physics space's default gravity points at the anchor (inverse square from its center), so plain [RigidBody3D]s and [method CharacterBody3D.get_gravity] need no [Area3D]. Without bodies the project's gravity is restored. [b]Frame switching[/b] ([code]universe/frame_switching[/code], on by default): bodies are placed from time in double precision, never stepped, and the scene shows them relative to the anchor. Below the anchor's rotating frame height ([member JarCelestialBody.rotating_frame_height]) the scene turns with it: the anchor stands still (also when it spins or orbits) and everything else moves around it, including the sky ([member Environment.sky_rotation]) and the [DirectionalLight3D]s not on a body (unless a [JarBodyLight] star drives them), so physics near the viewer happens on ground that does not move and its colliders are never moved. Higher up only the anchor's center stands still: the sky stays put and the anchor turns below. Switching between the two works like an anchor switch. When the anchor changes (flying from a planet to its moon), the new anchor stops exactly where it is: nothing jumps. Free [RigidBody3D]s and [CharacterBody3D]s keep moving as they did, their velocities converted into the new anchor's frame; bodies in the group [code]"jar_frame_exempt"[/code] are left alone (for controllers that already move along with a body, using [method get_body_velocity_at]). Relative poses are always recomputed from the universe, so switching back and forth never drifts. Off: bodies move in the scene as placed in the universe (the anchor spins and orbits too). All of this runs only in the game, not in the editor.

method.name: get_anchor
method.description: The body whose frame physics runs in (see the description).

method.name: get_anchor_override
method.description: The anchor set with [method set_anchor_override], or [code]null[/code].

method.name: get_body_angular_velocity
method.description: How fast [param body] turns in the scene (axis times radians per second), over the last physics tick. Zero for the frame anchor.

method.name: get_body_velocity_at
method.description: The scene velocity of a point at [param global_position] carried along by [param body] (its orbit and spin, as seen in the scene), over the last physics tick. For example, to keep a ship's velocity when it starts following a body: [code]velocity += get_body_velocity_at(old, position) - get_body_velocity_at(new, position)[/code].

method.name: get_bodies
method.description: All celestial bodies in the tree.

method.name: get_dominant_body
method.description: The body pulling hardest at [param global_position], or [code]null[/code] without bodies.

method.name: get_frame_anchor
method.description: The body the scene is currently relative to: it stands still. [code]null[/code] with frame switching off.

method.name: get_gravity
method.description: Gravity at [param global_position]. With [code]gravity/physical_strength[/code] on: the sum of all bodies' pull, minus the pull the anchor itself falls with (so far bodies only add their tides). Off: only the dominant body's pull. Without bodies: the project's gravity. For something that moves along with another body than the anchor (a character standing on a moving moon, following it), pass that body as [param relative_to]: the gravity is then relative to its free fall instead. With [param frame_relative] off: the bodies' pulls as they are, with no frame correction. That is smooth everywhere and does not change when the anchor switches, so use it to orient things in free flight (it is not the right acceleration for motion in the scene).

method.name: get_up
method.description: Up at [param global_position]: away from the same pulls as [method get_gravity] (in the anchor's frame, or [param relative_to]'s, other bodies only add their tides), each weighted by its strength to the power [code]gravity/up_sharpness[/code], so the dominant body decides and a nearby moon does not tilt the ground. [param fallback] where there is no pull. [param frame_relative] as in [method get_gravity].

method.name: is_frame_rotating
method.description: Whether the scene currently turns with the frame anchor (the viewer is near its surface), see the description.

method.name: has_bodies
method.description: Whether any [JarCelestialBody] is in the tree.

method.name: set_anchor_override
method.description: Forces the anchor; [code]null[/code] chooses it automatically again.

method.name: set_ticks
method.description: Sets the tick count (e.g. from a server or a save game). Bodies move to the new time on the next physics frame.

signal.name: anchor_changed
signal.description: The scene became relative to [param current] (frame switching). [param previous] is [code]null[/code] for the first anchor.
